/.title: Introduction
/.summary: Welcome to the PULSE developer documentation, for merchants with a PULSE account and subscription. Connect your catalogue and storefront, find the missing product information that costs sale

/api.title: What PULSE offers
/api.summary: Every API sold as a product, which calls count toward usage, and where the SDK stops.

/api/v1.title: Authentication
/api/v1.summary: One header, one base URL, and which credential opens what.

topics.heading: What a publishable key cannot do

/api/v1/audit.title: Audit a catalogue
/api/v1/audit.summary: POST /catalog/audit and /catalog/verify, which grade catalogue data rather than rank it.

/api/v1/decide.title: Decide for an agent
/api/v1/decide.summary: POST /decide tells an AI agent which candidate products meet a shopper's requirements, which fail, and which the listing cannot tell, with the missing facts named.

/api/v1/errors.title: Errors
/api/v1/errors.summary: The real response shape, and what each code means.

topics.heading: Two that are worth knowing apart

/api/v1/exposure.title: Record exposure
/api/v1/exposure.summary: POST /exposure, which is what makes ranking quality measurable.

/api/v1/interventions.title: Promotion Audit API
/api/v1/interventions.summary: POST /interventions/audit, /decide and /landed. Judge offers on orders kept after returns and failed deliveries, choose per group including giving nothing, and compare landed prices.

/api/v1/outcomes.title: Report order outcomes
/api/v1/outcomes.summary: POST /outcomes, which tells PULSE what happened to each order line, so ranking can favour the purchases that stay bought.

/api/v1/session.title: Read the session
/api/v1/session.summary: POST /session, which returns the personas inferred so far.

/api/v1/track.title: Send signals
/api/v1/track.summary: POST /track, the call everything else depends on.

/api/versioning.title: Versioning
/api/versioning.summary: What is versioned, what is not, and what happens when something changes.

topics.heading: The API is versioned. The guides are not.

/backend.title: Overview
/backend.summary: PULSE from a server, in any language that can send JSON over HTTPS.

topics.heading: Which calls belong on a server
One thing to get right first

/backend/csharp.title: C# and .NET
/backend/csharp.summary: A typed HttpClient, registered once, injected where it is needed.

/backend/go.title: Go
/backend/go.summary: net/http and encoding/json. Nothing to install.

/backend/java.title: Java
/backend/java.summary: java.net.http, in the JDK since 11. No dependencies beyond a JSON library.

/backend/nodejs.title: Node.js
/backend/nodejs.summary: The SDK runs on the server too, and fetch is there if you would rather not install it.

/backend/php.title: PHP
/backend/php.summary: cURL from the standard library, and Guzzle where a framework already ships it.

/backend/python.title: Python
/backend/python.summary: requests or httpx, plus where the call belongs in Django and FastAPI.

/backend/ruby.title: Ruby
/backend/ruby.summary: net/http from the standard library. Nothing to add to the Gemfile.

/backend/rust.title: Rust
/backend/rust.summary: reqwest and serde, with the client built once and cloned.

/catalogue.title: Catalogue products
/catalogue.summary: Four PULSE products that work on your product data, not your traffic. Find the missing facts that cost buying decisions, fix them in the right order, prove the fix, and keep it fixed.

topics.heading: The order they are used in

/catalogue/decision-audit.title: Decision Audit
/catalogue/decision-audit.summary: The PULSE Decision Audit ranks the missing product facts in your catalogue by how many buying decisions they cost, so your team fixes the right column first. One API call, one CSV.

/catalogue/decision-monitor.title: Decision Monitor
/catalogue/decision-monitor.summary: PULSE Decision Monitor compares each new catalogue export with the last and tells you which shelf slipped and why, before shoppers notice. Recurring, from one API call.

/catalogue/decision-verification.title: Decision Verification
/catalogue/decision-verification.summary: PULSE Decision Verification re-measures your catalogue after a repair and grades every claimed fix against what actually changed. Proof without waiting for traffic.

/catalogue/promotion-audit.title: Promotion Audit
/catalogue/promotion-audit.summary: PULSE Promotion Audit judges your vouchers, price cuts and free-shipping offers on the orders that stayed bought, after returns and failed deliveries, against doing nothing.

topics.heading: Settings, and where they come from

/catalogue/return-verification.title: Return Verification
/catalogue/return-verification.summary: PULSE Return Verification shows which missing product facts go with your returns, whether a repair moved them, and what that was worth at your own costs. Report order outcomes with one free

/changelog.title: Documentation changelog
/changelog.summary: Every change to these pages, newest first, read from git at build time rather than written by hand.

/concepts/how-it-works.title: How inference works
/concepts/how-it-works.summary: Signals in, personas out, your catalogue ranked against them.

/concepts/sessions.title: Sessions
/concepts/sessions.summary: How long a session lives, what identifies it, and how to reset one.

/concepts/signals.title: Signals
/concepts/signals.summary: What you send, what is captured for you, and what is deliberately not a signal.

/concepts/what-the-audit-measures.title: What the audit measures
/concepts/what-the-audit-measures.summary: Why the emptiest column is usually the wrong one to fix, what a bit of decision information buys, and the three cases where the ranking is wrong.

/frameworks.title: Overview
/frameworks.summary: One core, no framework coupling. Three need an adapter pattern, three need nothing.

/frameworks/alpine.title: Alpine
/frameworks/alpine.summary: No build step. The global, used straight from HTML attributes.

/frameworks/angular.title: Angular
/frameworks/angular.summary: An injectable service, initialised once the browser is running.

/frameworks/astro.title: Astro
/frameworks/astro.summary: Islands use the React or Vue guide. A plain page is one script tag.

/frameworks/laravel.title: Laravel
/frameworks/laravel.summary: A Blade partial for the browser half. Secrets stay on the server.

/frameworks/react.title: React and Next.js
/frameworks/react.summary: Create the client once, share it, and keep init() in the browser.

/frameworks/vue.title: Vue and Nuxt
/frameworks/vue.summary: A plugin, provided to the app, guarded against SSR.

/going-live.title: Going live
/going-live.summary: What to check before you ship PULSE, what to watch in the first week, and the claims we will not make for you.

topics.heading: What should I check before shipping?
What should I check before shipping?

/mcp.title: MCP for agents
/mcp.summary: Connect PULSE to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client, so an agent searches the documentation instead of guessing, and asks the Decision API which products really meet a shopper's requi

topics.heading: How does an agent decide with it?

/platforms.title: Overview
/platforms.summary: What works on a hosted storefront today, and what is still a script tag rather than an app.

/platforms/magento.title: Magento 2
/platforms/magento.summary: Layout XML and a template block, which is how Magento adds a script.

/platforms/shopify.title: Shopify
/platforms/shopify.summary: One script tag in theme.liquid, and signals built from Liquid objects.

/platforms/wordpress.title: WordPress and WooCommerce
/platforms/wordpress.summary: wp_enqueue_script in a small plugin, with signals from the WooCommerce conditionals.

topics.heading: Write it as a plugin, not a theme edit

/quickstart.title: Quick start
/quickstart.summary: From nothing to a ranked catalogue in about ten lines.

/sdk.title: SDK reference
/sdk.summary: Every method on PulseClient, the config it takes, and the functions the package exports beside it.

/storefront.title: Storefront products
/storefront.summary: PULSE storefront products rank your catalogue for each live visit, anonymously. Decision API, Search, Recommendations and category pages, each with the reason behind every score.

topics.heading: Built to run beside what you have

/storefront/category-pages.title: Category pages
/storefront/category-pages.summary: PULSE orders category and landing-page grids for whoever arrived, so a campaign that sends a thousand people to one page shows each of them the products they came for.

/storefront/decision-api.title: Decision API
/storefront/decision-api.summary: The PULSE Decision API reads an anonymous visit as it happens and says what the shopper is shopping for, so every ranking call that follows is personal from the first click.

/storefront/recommendations.title: Recommendations
/storefront/recommendations.summary: PULSE Recommendations rank a strip against the visit happening now, so a first-time shopper gets relevant picks without any purchase history. One call, alongside the page it sits on.

/storefront/search.title: Search
/storefront/search.summary: PULSE Search ranks results on what the shopper is deciding, not only on matching words. Keep your search engine and rerank its results, or let PULSE rank the products you pass in. Reads Viet

topics.heading: Queries in the shopper's own words

/vi.title: Giới thiệu
/vi.summary: Chào mừng bạn đến với tài liệu dành cho nhà phát triển của PULSE, dành cho nhà bán hàng đã có tài khoản PULSE và gói đăng ký. Kết nối danh mục và cửa hàng, tìm ra thông tin sản phẩm còn thiế

/vi/changelog.title: Lịch sử tài liệu
/vi/changelog.summary: Mọi thay đổi trên các trang này, mới nhất trước, đọc trực tiếp từ git khi dựng site chứ không viết tay.

topics.heading: Xem lịch sử của từng trang

/vi/mcp.title: MCP cho tác tử
/vi/mcp.summary: Kết nối tài liệu PULSE với Claude, Cursor hoặc bất kỳ MCP client nào, để tác tử tìm và đọc đúng trang thay vì đoán.

topics.heading: Tác tử ra quyết định với nó như thế nào?
